Wildlife Troopers responded and investigated the scene. Troopers determined that the muskox was shot illegally, and no efforts were made to salvage any of the meat. Through the service of search warrants and interviews Troopers determined 42-year-old Lower Kalskag resident Joseph Kameroff killed the muskox. title: AST Attempted Murder: Fairbanks [AK25128943]
summary: On December 31, 2025, at 5:55 am, Alaska State Troopers received a report of a man who had been shot on Winch Road in Fairbanks. The man fled to a nearby residence after being shot by Theodore Samsa, age 42, of Fairbanks. Troopers arrived on scene and made contact with the victim, who stated Samsa had shot him. While on scene, troopers heard gunshots coming from the incident location. Samsa barricaded himself in the residence and refused commands to surrender. He shot several times inside the residence, as well as trying to shoot at troopers on scene. SWAT deployed less lethal munitions, and Samsa eventually surrendered and was taken into custody. The victim was taken to a local hospital and is expected to survive. Samsa was arrested for Attempted Murder I and Assault I.

title: AST Failure To Salvage Moose: Farewell GMU 19C [AK25091599]
summary: On 09/08/2025, McGrath AWT contacted two hunters with a dead 52" bull moose at the Farewell Strip. Investigation determined Jeffery Harris, age 42 of Anchorage, took the moose on the evening of September 5th. The moose was left in the field for approximately 14 hours before being field dressed. Temperatures throughout the region were warm and wet. The meat of the moose spoiled due to not being properly cared for in a timely manner. Investigation also determined Harris took the two front shoulders, and other chunks of meat, and discarded them in the brush due to their putrid smell and colors. Harris was issued a citation for failing to salvage all edible meat. The moose rack and rotten meat were seized as evidence. Arraignment was set for October 9, 2025, in the Aniak Court.

Despite these efforts, Foreman was declared deceased at the facility. His next of kin have been notified, and his body has been sent to the State Medical Examiner’s Office for autopsy.

title: AST Fail to Yield: Seward [AK25027493]
summary: On 03/25/2025, Seward AST initiated a traffic stop at approximately 71 Mile of the Seward Highway on a blue Honda CRV that was traveling 84 MPH in a 65 MPH zone. When turning around on the vehicle, the vehicle accelerated and failed to yield. Thusly a pursuit was initiated. The vehicle drove upwards of 100 MPH during the pursuit, drove erratically, and went into the opposing lane of travel multiple times. The driver nearly went head on with a semi-truck driver. While in pursuit, AST learned that the vehicle was just recently stolen out of the Girdwood area. A tire deflation device was used at approximately 45 mile of the Seward Highway, which was set by another member of Seward AST. The vehicle continued attempting to elude but was ultimately blocked/pinned in by three members of Seward AS

title: AST Snowmachine/Musher collision: Galena [AK20015147]
summary: Update: The driver of snowmachine contacted AST and is cooperating with the ongoing investigation. Original Text: On 3/2/2020, Alaska State Troopers in Galena received a report that a musher who was participating in the Serum Run was struck the night prior, at approximately 2030 hours, by a snowmachiner about five miles outside of Galena. Investigation revealed that Kirsten Bey, 64 of Nome, was mushing to Galena from Ruby when she was struck by an unknown snowmachiner. Another participant, riding snowmachine, came upon the scene shortly after and helped transport Bey to Galena. The snowmachiner that hit the musher remained on scene until Bey was transported away. Bey was medivaced from Galena to the Fairbanks Medical Hospital with significant injuries. The incident is under investigation.
